scanner_doubts: qe-math-002 - `unpleasant.md:271` is a false positive, and the cause is a lookbehind that stops one token too early. The `supT` regex in `check_math_002` (`tools/qestyle_rules.py`) accepts as a transpose base either a `DECORATED` group or a bare capital guarded by `(?<![A-Za-z0-9\\])`. `DECORATED` is `\\(?:hat|tilde|bar|vec|widehat|widetilde|mathbf|boldsymbol|check|dot)\{[^{}]*\}` - it requires braces - so the brace-less `\widetilde R` is not seen as decorated, and the bare-capital branch then matches the `R`, because the character before it is a space and the lookbehind only blocks an immediately preceding backslash. With ` B_{-1}` following, the factor lookahead is satisfied and `R^T` is reported. But `\widetilde R^T B_{-1}` at 271 is compounding, not transposition: line 82 says "Let $\widetilde R > 1$ be a time-invariant gross real rate of return on government one-period inflation-indexed bonds", and the code writes it `R_tilde ** T * Bm1` at 370, 440 and 556. (The second `\widetilde R^T` on the same line escapes only by accident - it is followed by `}`, so the factor lookahead fails.) I tested a stopgap in a scratch copy: add `(?<!\\tilde )(?<!\\widetilde )(?<!\\bar )(?<!\\hat )` to the bare-capital branch and re-run over all five series - 34 hits -> 33, nothing added, and the single suppressed hit is exactly this one. So it is safe on today's corpus, but I would not merge it as the fix: it is the wrong discriminator, because `\bar A^T B` for a genuine transpose of a decorated matrix is a shape this corpus could acquire tomorrow, and the exemption would silence it. The right discriminator is the one the prose already supplies - a symbol declared as a rate or compared to a number is a scalar, so `^T` on it is a power - and the cheap approximation of it is to require the base of a bare-capital `^T` to be a symbol the file uses with a matrix-like index somewhere. I flag this so the false positive is on record; the DECORATED branch itself is behaving correctly (all 18 of its corpus hits are `\vec{\mu}^T`-style transposes in `calvo_machine_learn`, in both `lecture-dp` and `lecture-python-advanced.myst`). Note this is independent of the `)^T` gap I filed under `time_series_with_matrices`: tightening the superscript spelling there leaves this hit exactly where it is, which I confirmed (that branch stays at 34 before the lookbehind change)
